shloka_text: ततो रामो महातेजा विस्मयात्पुनरेव हि । उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम् ।। 7.31.1 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmo mahātejā vismayātpunareva hi | uvāca praṇato vākyamagastyamṛṣisattamam || 7.31.1 ||
translation: ततो then, रामः Rama, महातेजा the greatly effulgent one, विस्मयात् out of wonder, पुनरेव again indeed, हि indeed, उवाच spoke, प्रणतः bowing down, वाक्यम् words, अगस्त्यम् to Agastya, ऋषिसत्तमम् the best among sages
explanation: Then, the greatly effulgent Rama, filled with wonder, again spoke words to Agastya, the best among sages, bowing down to him.
comments: Rama asks whether no king ever humbled Ravana, and Agastya begins the tale of Kartavirya Arjuna -- Ravana reaches Mahishmati to find its king Arjuna away sporting in the Narmada -- coming to the river himself, Ravana bathes and sets up a Shiva-linga on the sandbank, worshipping it with flowers, song and dance.

shloka_text: भगवन्राक्षसः क्रूरो यदाप्रभृति मेदिनीम् । पर्यटत्किं तदा लोकाः शून्या आसन्द्विजोत्तम ।। 7.31.2 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanrākṣasaḥ krūro yadāprabhṛti medinīm | paryaṭatkiṃ tadā lokāḥ śūnyā āsandvijottama || 7.31.2 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, राक्षसः the demon, क्रूरः cruel, यदाप्रभृति from when, मेदिनीम् the earth, पर्यटत् roamed, किम् whether, तदा then, लोकाः the worlds (people), शून्याः empty, आसन् were, द्विजोत्तम O best among twice-born (Brahmins)
explanation: O revered one, O best among Brahmins, when that cruel demon roamed the earth, were the worlds then empty of people?

shloka_text: राजा वा राजमात्रो वा किं तदा नात्र कश्चन । धर्षणं यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।। 7.31.3 ।।
transliteration: rājā vā rājamātro vā kiṃ tadā nātra kaścana | dharṣaṇaṃ yatra na prāpto rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ || 7.31.3 ||
translation: राजा a king, वा or, राजमात्रः a king's minister/equal to a king, वा or, किम् whether, तदा then, न not, अत्र here, कश्चन anyone, धर्षणम् humiliation/defeat, यत्र where, न not, प्राप्तः obtained/met, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of demons
explanation: Or was there no king or king's equal then, where Ravana, the lord of demons, did not meet with defeat or humiliation?

shloka_text: उताहो हतवीर्यास्ते बभूवुः पृथिवीक्षितः । बहिष्कृता वरास्त्रैश्च बहवो निर्जिता नृपाः ।। 7.31.4 ।।
transliteration: utāho hatavīryāste babhūvuḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ | bahiṣkṛtā varāstraiśca bahavo nirjitā nṛpāḥ || 7.31.4 ||
translation: उताहो or perhaps, हतवीर्याः whose valor was destroyed, ते those, बभूवुः became, पृथिवीक्षितः kings (earth-rulers), बहिष्कृताः expelled/deprived, वरास्त्रैः by excellent weapons, च and, बहवः many, निर्जिताः conquered, नृपाः kings
explanation: Or perhaps those kings became devoid of valor, and many rulers were conquered and deprived of their excellent weapons.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ह्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः । उवाच रामं प्रहसन्पितामह इवेश्वरम् ।। 7.31.5 ।।
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā hyagastyo bhagavānṛṣiḥ | uvāca rāmaṃ prahasanpitāmaha iveśvaram || 7.31.5 ||
translation: राघवस्य of Rama (descendant of Raghu), वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, हि indeed, अगस्त्यः Agastya, भगवान् the revered, ऋषिः sage, उवाच spoke, रामम् to Rama, प्रहसन् laughing, पितामहः grandfather (Brahma), इव like, ईश्वरम् to the lord (Shiva/Vishnu)
explanation: Having heard the words of Rama, the revered sage Agastya, laughing, spoke to Rama as Brahma would speak to the Lord.

shloka_text: इत्येवं बाधमानस्तु पार्थिवान्पार्थिवर्षभ । चचार रावणो राम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते ।। 7.31.6 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ bādhamānastu pārthivānpārthivarṣabha | cacāra rāvaṇo rāma pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpate || 7.31.6 ||
translation: इत्येवं thus, बाधमानस्तु indeed oppressing, पार्थिवान् kings, पार्थिवर्षभ O best of kings, चचार roamed, रावणो Ravana, राम O Rama, पृथिवीं the earth, पृथिवीपते O lord of the earth.
explanation: O Rama, O best of kings, O lord of the earth, Ravana thus indeed roamed the earth, oppressing kings.

shloka_text: ततो माहिष्मतीं नाम पुरीं स्वर्गपुरीप्रभाम् । सम्प्राप्तो यत्र सान्निध्यं सदासीद्वसुरेतसः ।। 7.31.7 ।।
transliteration: tato māhiṣmatīṃ nāma purīṃ svargapurīprabhām | samprāpto yatra sānnidhyaṃ sadāsīdvasuretasaḥ || 7.31.7 ||
translation: ततो then, माहिष्मतीं Mahishmati, नाम named, पुरीं city, स्वर्गपुरीप्रभाम् shining like a city of heaven, सम्प्राप्तो reached, यत्र where, सान्निध्यं presence, सदासीत् always was, वसुरेतसः of Vasuretasa.
explanation: Then he reached the city named Mahishmati, which shone like a celestial city, and where the presence of Vasuretasa (Agni) always resided.

shloka_text: तुल्य आसीन्नृपस्तस्य प्रभावाद्वसुरेतसः । अर्जुनो नाम यत्राग्निः शरकुण्डेशयः सदा ।। 7.31.8 ।।
transliteration: tulya āsīnnṛpastasya prabhāvādvasuretasaḥ | arjuno nāma yatrāgniḥ śarakuṇḍeśayaḥ sadā || 7.31.8 ||
translation: तुल्य equal, आसीत् was, नृपस्तस्य its king, प्रभावात् by the might, वसुरेतसः of Vasuretasa, अर्जुनो Arjuna, नाम named, यत्राग्निः where Agni, शरकुण्डेशयः residing in a pond of arrows, सदा always.
explanation: Its king, named Arjuna, was equal in might to Vasuretasa (Agni), where Agni always resided, known as Sharakuṇḍeśaya.

shloka_text: तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ हैहयाधिपतिर्बली । अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः ।। 7.31.9 ।।
transliteration: tameva divasaṃ so 'tha haihayādhipatirbalī | arjuno narmadāṃ rantuṃ gataḥ strībhiḥ saheśvaraḥ || 7.31.9 ||
translation: तमेव that very, दिवसं day, सो ऽथ he then, हैहयाधिपतिर्बली the powerful lord of the Haihayas, अर्जुनो Arjuna, नर्मदां to the Narmada, रन्तुं to sport, गतः went, स्त्रीभिः with women, सहेश्वरः with his wives.
explanation: On that very day, the powerful lord of the Haihayas, Arjuna, had gone to the Narmada river with his wives to sport.

shloka_text: तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ रावणस्तत्र आगतः । रावणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत ।। 7.31.10 ।।
transliteration: tameva divasaṃ so 'tha rāvaṇastatra āgataḥ | rāvaṇo rākṣasendrastu tasyāmātyānapṛcchata || 7.31.10 ||
translation: तमेव that very, दिवसं day, सो ऽथ he then, रावणस्तत्र Ravana there, आगतः arrived, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु the lord of Rakshasas indeed, तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत asked his ministers.
explanation: On that very day, Ravana arrived there, and the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, then inquired of his ministers.

shloka_text: क्वार्जुनो नृपतिः शीघ्रं सम्यगाख्यातुमर्हथ । रावणो ऽहमनुप्राप्तो युद्धेप्सुर्नृवरेण ह । ममागमनमप्यग्रे युष्माभिः सन्निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.31.11 ।।
transliteration: kvārjuno nṛpatiḥ śīghraṃ samyagākhyātumarhatha | rāvaṇo 'hamanuprāpto yuddhepsurnṛvareṇa ha | mamāgamanamapyagre yuṣmābhiḥ sannivedyatām || 7.31.11 ||
translation: क्व where, अर्जुनो Arjuna, नृपतिः the king, शीघ्रं quickly, सम्यक् properly, आख्यातुम् to tell, अर्हथ you ought; रावणो Ravana, अहम् I, अनुप्राप्तो have arrived, युद्धेप्सुः desirous of battle, नृवरेण with the best of men, ह indeed; मम my, आगमनम् arrival, अपि also, अग्रे before him, युष्माभिः by you all, सन्निवेद्यताम् let it be announced.
explanation: Ravana asks Arjuna's attendants to quickly and properly inform him of Arjuna's whereabouts, declaring his own arrival as Ravana, desirous of battle with the best of men, and instructing them to announce his presence to the king.

shloka_text: इत्येवं रावणेनोक्तास्ते ऽमात्याः सुविपश्चितः । अब्रुवन्राक्षसपतिमसान्निध्यं महीपतेः ।। 7.31.12 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ rāvaṇenoktāste 'mātyāḥ suvipaścitaḥ | abruvanrākṣasapatimasānnidhyaṃ mahīpateḥ || 7.31.12 ||
translation: इति thus, एवं in this manner, रावणेन by Ravana, उक्ताः spoken to, ते those, अमात्याः ministers, सुविपश्चितः very wise, अब्रुवन् they said, राक्षसपतिम् to the lord of Rakshasas, असान्निध्यम् the absence, महीपतेः of the king.
explanation: Thus addressed by Ravana, those very wise ministers informed the lord of Rakshasas about the king's absence.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा विश्रवसः पुत्रः पौराणामर्जुनं गतम् । अपसृत्यागतो विन्ध्यं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् ।। 7.31.13 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā viśravasaḥ putraḥ paurāṇāmarjunaṃ gatam | apasṛtyāgato vindhyaṃ himavatsannibhaṃ girim || 7.31.13 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, विश्रवसः of Vishravas, पुत्रः the son, पौराणाम् from the citizens, अर्जुनं Arjuna, गतम् had gone, अपसृत्य having departed, आगतो he came, विन्ध्यं to the Vindhya, हिमवत् like the Himalayas, सन्निभं resembling, गिरिम् mountain.
explanation: Having heard from the citizens that Arjuna had departed, Ravana, the son of Vishravas, also departed and came to the Vindhya mountain, which resembled the Himalayas.

shloka_text: स तमभ्रमिवाविष्टमुद्भ्रन्तमिव मेदिनीम् । अपश्यद्रावणो विन्ध्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम् ।। 7.31.14 ।।
transliteration: sa tamabhramivāviṣṭamudbhrantamiva medinīm | apaśyadrāvaṇo vindhyamālikhantamivāmbaram || 7.31.14 ||
translation: सः he, तम् that, अभ्रम् a cloud, इव like, आविष्टम् pervaded, उद्भ्रान्तम् bewildered, इव like, मेदिनीम् the earth; अपश्यत् he saw, रावणो Ravana, विन्ध्यम् the Vindhya, आलिखन्तम् scratching, इव as if, अम्बरम् the sky.
explanation: Ravana saw that Vindhya mountain, which seemed to pervade the clouds and bewilder the earth, as if it were scratching the sky.

shloka_text: सहस्रशिखरोपेतं सिंहाध्युषितकन्दरम् । प्रपातपतितैस्तोयैः साट्टहासमिवाम्बुधिम् ।। 7.31.15 ।।
transliteration: sahasraśikharopetaṃ siṃhādhyuṣitakandaram | prapātapatitaistoyaiḥ sāṭṭahāsamivāmbudhim || 7.31.15 ||
translation: सहस्र a thousand, शिखर peaks, उपेतं endowed with, सिंह by lions, अध्युषित inhabited, कन्दरम् caves; प्रपात from waterfalls, पतितैः fallen, तोयैः by waters, स with, अट्टहासम् loud laughter, इव like, अम्बुधिम् the ocean.
explanation: He saw the mountain endowed with a thousand peaks, its caves inhabited by lions, and its waters falling from waterfalls, resembling the ocean with its loud laughter.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वैः साप्सरोगणकिन्नरैः । स्वस्त्रीभिः क्रीडमानैश्च स्वर्गभूतं महोच्छ्रयम् ।। 7.31.16 ।।
transliteration: devadānavagandharvaiḥ sāpsarogaṇakinnaraiḥ | svastrībhiḥ krīḍamānaiśca svargabhūtaṃ mahocchrayam || 7.31.16 ||
translation: देवदानवगन्धर्वैः by gods, demons, and gandharvas, साप्सरोगणकिन्नरैः with groups of apsaras and kinnaras, स्वस्त्रीभिः with their own wives, क्रीडमानैः playing, च and, स्वर्गभूतम् appearing like heaven, महोच्छ्रयम् of great height.
explanation: The mountain, of immense height, appeared like heaven itself, with gods, demons, gandharvas, apsaras, and kinnaras playing there with their wives.

shloka_text: नदीभिः स्यन्दमानाभिः स्फटिकप्रतिमं जलम् । फणाभिश्चलजिह्वाभिरनन्तमिव विष्ठितम् ।। 7.31.17 ।।
transliteration: nadībhiḥ syandamānābhiḥ sphaṭikapratimaṃ jalam | phaṇābhiścalajihvābhiranantamiva viṣṭhitam || 7.31.17 ||
translation: नदीभिः by rivers, स्यन्दमानाभिः flowing, स्फटिकप्रतिमम् crystal-like, जलम् water, फणाभिः with hoods, चलजिह्वाभिः with flickering tongues, अनन्तम् Ananta, इव as if, विष्ठितम् pervaded.
explanation: The mountain was pervaded by crystal-clear water from flowing rivers, and appeared as if Ananta, the serpent god with his hoods and flickering tongues, had spread himself across it.

shloka_text: उत्क्रामन्तं दरीवन्तं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् । पश्यमानस्ततो विन्ध्यं रावणो नर्मदां ययौ ।। 7.31.18 ।।
transliteration: utkrāmantaṃ darīvantaṃ himavatsannibhaṃ girim | paśyamānastato vindhyaṃ rāvaṇo narmadāṃ yayau || 7.31.18 ||
translation: उत्क्रामन्तम् rising high, दरीवन्तम् having caves, हिमवत्सन्निभम् resembling the Himalayas, गिरिम् mountain, पश्यमानः seeing, ततः then, विन्ध्यम् the Vindhya, रावणः Ravana, नर्मदाम् to the Narmada, ययौ went.
explanation: Ravana, after observing the Vindhya mountain, which rose high, possessed many caves, and resembled the Himalayas, then proceeded to the Narmada river.

shloka_text: चलोपलजलां पुण्यां पश्चिमोदधिगामिनीम् ।। 7.31.19 ।।
transliteration: calopalajalāṃ puṇyāṃ paścimodadhigāminīm || 7.31.19 ||
translation: चलोपलजलाम् whose water moved over pebbles, पुण्याम् sacred, पश्चिमोदधिगामिनीम् flowing towards the western ocean.
explanation: Ravana went to the Narmada river, which was sacred, had water agitated by moving pebbles, and flowed towards the western ocean.

shloka_text: महिषैः सृमरैः सिंहैः शार्दूलर्क्षगजोत्तमैः । उष्णाभितप्तैस्तृषितैः सङ्क्षोभितजलाशयाम् ।। 7.31.20 ।।
transliteration: mahiṣaiḥ sṛmaraiḥ siṃhaiḥ śārdūlarkṣagajottamaiḥ | uṣṇābhitaptaistṛṣitaiḥ saṅkṣobhitajalāśayām || 7.31.20 ||
translation: महिषैः by buffaloes, सृमरैः by sṛmara deer, सिंहैः by lions, शार्दूलर्क्षगजोत्तमैः by tigers, bears, and excellent elephants, उष्णाभितप्तैः tormented by heat, तृषितैः thirsty, सङ्क्षोभितजलाशयाम् whose waters were agitated.
explanation: The Narmada's waters were agitated by buffaloes, sṛmara deer, lions, tigers, bears, and magnificent elephants, all of whom were tormented by the heat and seeking to quench their thirst.

shloka_text: चक्रवाकैः सकारण्डैः सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः । सारसैश्च सदा मत्तैः सुकूजद्भिः समावृताम् ।। 7.31.21 ।।
transliteration: cakravākaiḥ sakāraṇḍaiḥ sahaṃsajalakukkuṭaiḥ | sārasaiśca sadā mattaiḥ sukūjadbhiḥ samāvṛtām || 7.31.21 ||
translation: चक्रवाकैः by chakravaka birds, सकारण्डैः with karanda ducks, सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः with swans and water-hens, सारसैश्च and by sarasa cranes, सदा always, मत्तैः intoxicated (joyful), सुकूजद्भिः sweetly cooing, समावृताम् surrounded.
explanation: The river was surrounded by chakravaka birds, karanda ducks, swans, water-hens, and sarasa cranes, all always joyful and sweetly cooing.

shloka_text: फुल्लद्रुमकृतोत्तंसां चक्रवाकयुगस्तनीम् । विस्तीर्णपुलिनश्रोणीं हंसावलिसुमेखलाम् ।। 7.31.22 ।।
transliteration: phulladrumakṛtottaṃsāṃ cakravākayugastanīm | vistīrṇapulinaśroṇīṃ haṃsāvalisumekhalām || 7.31.22 ||
translation: फुल्लद्रुमकृतोत्तंसां having blooming trees as her head-ornaments, चक्रवाकयुगस्तनीम् having a pair of chakravaka birds as her breasts, विस्तीर्णपुलिनश्रोणीं having wide sandbanks as her hips, हंसावलिसुमेखलाम् having rows of swans as her beautiful girdle.
explanation: The river was adorned with blooming trees like head-ornaments, pairs of chakravaka birds like breasts, wide sandbanks like hips, and rows of swans like a beautiful girdle.

shloka_text: पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गीं जलफेनामलांशुकाम् । जलावगाहसंस्पर्शां फुल्लोत्पलशुभेक्षणाम् । पुष्पकादवरुह्याशु नर्मदां सरितां वराम् ।। 7.31.23 ।।
transliteration: puṣpareṇvanuliptāṅgīṃ jalaphenāmalāṃśukām | jalāvagāhasaṃsparśāṃ phullotpalaśubhekṣaṇām | puṣpakādavaruhyāśu narmadāṃ saritāṃ varām || 7.31.23 ||
translation: पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गीं having her body smeared with pollen, जलफेनामलांशुकाम् having pure foam of water as her garment, जलावगाहसंस्पर्शां whose touch was like bathing in water, फुल्लोत्पलशुभेक्षणाम् having blooming lotuses as her auspicious eyes, पुष्पकादवरुह्याशु quickly descending from the Pushpaka, नर्मदां to the Narmada, सरितां वराम् the best of rivers.
explanation: With her body smeared with pollen, pure water foam as her garment, a refreshing touch like a bath, and auspicious eyes like blooming lotuses, Ravana quickly descended from the Pushpaka to the Narmada, the best of rivers.

shloka_text: इष्टामिव वरां नारीमवगाह्य दशाननः । स तस्याः पुलिने रम्ये नानामुनिनिषेविते ।। 7.31.24 ।।
transliteration: iṣṭāmiva varāṃ nārīmavagāhya daśānanaḥ | sa tasyāḥ puline ramye nānāmuniniṣevite || 7.31.24 ||
translation: इष्टामिव like a desired, वरां excellent, नारीम् woman, अवगाह्य having entered, दशाननः Dashanana (Ravana), स he, तस्याः her, पुलिने on the sandbank, रम्ये beautiful, नानामुनिनिषेविते frequented by various sages.
explanation: Ravana, having entered the Narmada as if embracing a beloved woman, then sat on her beautiful sandbank, which was frequented by various sages.

shloka_text: उपोपविष्टैः सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसपुङ्गवः । प्रख्याय नर्मदां सो ऽथ गङ्गेयमिति रावणः ।। 7.31.25 ।।
transliteration: upopaviṣṭaiḥ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ | prakhyāya narmadāṃ so 'tha gaṅgeyamiti rāvaṇaḥ || 7.31.25 ||
translation: उपोपविष्टैः seated nearby, सचिवैः with his ministers, सार्धं together with, राक्षसपुङ्गवः the foremost of rakshasas (Ravana), प्रख्याय having declared, नर्मदां the Narmada, सः he, अथ then, गङ्गेयमिति "this is Ganga", रावणः Ravana.
explanation: The foremost of rakshasas, Ravana, then sat with his ministers who were seated nearby, mistakenly declaring the Narmada to be the Ganga.

shloka_text: नर्मदादर्शजं हर्षमाप्तवान् राक्षसाधिपः । उवाच सचिवांस्तत्र सलीलं शुकसारणौ ।। 7.31.26 ।।
transliteration: narmadādarśajaṃ harṣamāptavān rākṣasādhipaḥ | uvāca sacivāṃstatra salīlaṃ śukasāraṇau || 7.31.26 ||
translation: नर्मदादर्शजम् from seeing the Narmada, हर्षम् joy, आप्तवान् obtained, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of rakshasas, उवाच said, सचिवान् to his ministers, तत्र there, सलीलम् playfully, शुकसारणौ to Shuka and Sarana,
explanation: The lord of rakshasas, having experienced joy from seeing the Narmada, playfully spoke to his ministers Shuka and Sarana there.

shloka_text: एष रश्मिसहस्रेण जगत्कृत्वैव काञ्चनम् । तीक्ष्णतापकरः सूर्यो नभसो ऽर्धं समाश्रितः ।। 7.31.27 ।।
transliteration: eṣa raśmisahasreṇa jagatkṛtvaiva kāñcanam | tīkṣṇatāpakaraḥ sūryo nabhaso 'rdhaṃ samāśritaḥ || 7.31.27 ||
translation: एष this, रश्मिसहस्रेण with a thousand rays, जगत् the world, कृत्वैव having made indeed, काञ्चनम् golden, तीक्ष्णतापकरः causing intense heat, सूर्यः the sun, नभसः of the sky, अर्धम् half, समाश्रितः has occupied,
explanation: This sun, having made the world golden with its thousand rays and causing intense heat, has indeed reached the middle of the sky.

shloka_text: मामासीनं विदित्वैव चन्द्रायति दिवाकरः ।। 7.31.28 ।।
transliteration: māmāsīnaṃ viditvaiva candrāyati divākaraḥ || 7.31.28 ||
translation: माम् me, आसीनम् seated, विदित्वैव having known indeed, चन्द्रायति acts like the moon, दिवाकरः the sun,
explanation: The sun, knowing that I am seated here, indeed acts like the moon (becomes cool).

shloka_text: नर्मदाजलशीतश्च सुगन्धिः श्रमनाशनः । मद्भयादनिलो ऽप्यत्र वात्येष सुसमाहितः ।। 7.31.29 ।।
transliteration: narmadājalaśītaśca sugandhiḥ śramanāśanaḥ | madbhayādanilo 'pyatra vātyeṣa susamāhitaḥ || 7.31.29 ||
translation: नर्मदाजलशीतश्च and cool with Narmada's water, सुगन्धिः fragrant, श्रमनाशनः destroyer of fatigue, मद्भयात् from my fear, अनिलः the wind, अपि even, अत्र here, वाति blows, एष this, सुसमाहितः very carefully,
explanation: Even this wind, cool with the Narmada's water, fragrant, and a destroyer of fatigue, blows here very carefully out of fear of me.

shloka_text: इयं वापि सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा नर्मदा नर्मवर्धिनी । नक्रमीनविहङ्गोर्मिः सभयेवाङ्गना स्थिता ।। 7.31.30 ।।
transliteration: iyaṃ vāpi saricchreṣṭhā narmadā narmavardhinī | nakramīnavihaṅgormiḥ sabhayevāṅganā sthitā || 7.31.30 ||
translation: इयम् this, वा अपि or even, सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा best of rivers, नर्मदा Narmada, नर्मवर्धिनी increasing joy, नक्रमीनविहङ्गोर्मिः having crocodiles, fish, birds, and waves, सभयेव अङ्गना like a frightened woman, स्थिता stands,
explanation: This Narmada, the best of rivers and increaser of joy, with its crocodiles, fish, birds, and waves, stands as if a frightened woman.

shloka_text: तद्भवन्तः क्षताः शस्त्रैर्नृपैरिन्द्रसमैर्युधि । चन्दनस्य रसेनेव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः ।। 7.31.31 ।।
transliteration: tadbhavantaḥ kṣatāḥ śastrairnṛpairindrasamairyudhi | candanasya raseneva rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ || 7.31.31 ||
translation: तत् therefore, भवन्तः you, क्षताः wounded, शस्त्रैः by weapons, नृपैः by kings, इन्द्रसमैः equal to Indra, युधि in battle, चन्दनस्य of sandalwood, रसेन with the juice, इव as if, रुधिरेण with blood, समुक्षिताः drenched.
explanation: Therefore, you, who were wounded in battle by kings equal to Indra, are drenched in blood as if with sandalwood paste.

shloka_text: ते यूयमवगाहध्वं नर्मदां शर्मदां शुभाम् । महापद्ममुखा मत्ता गङ्गामिव गहागजाः । अस्यां स्नात्वा महानद्यां पाप्मानं विप्रमोक्ष्यथ ।। 7.31.32 ।।
transliteration: te yūyamavagāhadhvaṃ narmadāṃ śarmadāṃ śubhām | mahāpadmamukhā mattā gaṅgāmiva gahāgajāḥ | asyāṃ snātvā mahānadyāṃ pāpmānaṃ vipramokṣyatha || 7.31.32 ||
translation: ते those, यूयम् you, अवगाहध्वम् plunge into, नर्मदां the Narmada, शर्मदां bestowing happiness, शुभाम् auspicious, महापद्ममुखाः led by Mahapadma, मत्ताः intoxicated, गङ्गाम् into the Ganga, इव like, गहागजाः wild elephants; अस्याम् in this, स्नात्वा having bathed, महानद्याम् in the great river, पाप्मानम् sin, विप्रमोक्ष्यथ you will be freed from.
explanation: You should plunge into the auspicious and joy-giving Narmada river, just as rutting wild elephants led by Mahapadma plunge into the Ganga, and by bathing in this great river, you will be freed from sin.

shloka_text: अहमप्यद्य पुलिने शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे । पुष्पोपहारं शनकैः करिष्यामि कपर्दिनः ।। 7.31.33 ।।
transliteration: ahamapyadya puline śaradindusamaprabhe | puṣpopahāraṃ śanakaiḥ kariṣyāmi kapardinaḥ || 7.31.33 ||
translation: अहम् I, अपि also, अद्य today, पुलिने on the sandbank, शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे having the luster of the autumn moon, पुष्पोपहारम् a flower offering, शनकैः gently, करिष्यामि will make, कपर्दिनः to Kapardin (Shiva).
explanation: I also will gently make a flower offering to Kapardin (Shiva) today on the sandbank, which shines like the autumn moon.

shloka_text: रावणेनैवमुक्तास्तु प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः । समहोदरधूम्राक्षा नर्मदां विजगाहिरे ।। 7.31.34 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇenaivamuktāstu prahastaśukasāraṇāḥ | samahodaradhūmrākṣā narmadāṃ vijagāhire || 7.31.34 ||
translation: रावणेन by Ravana, एवम् thus, उक्ताः addressed, तु indeed, प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः Prahasta, Shuka, and Sarana, समहोदरधूम्राक्षाः along with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, नर्मदां into the Narmada, विजगाहिरे plunged.
explanation: Thus addressed by Ravana, Prahasta, Shuka, Sarana, along with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, plunged into the Narmada river.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रगजैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता नर्मदा नदी । वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैर्गङ्गा इव महागजैः ।। 7.31.35 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasendragajaistaistu kṣobhitā narmadā nadī | vāmanāñjanapadmādyairgaṅgā iva mahāgajaiḥ || 7.31.35 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द्रगजैः by those chief Rakshasas (who are like elephants), तैः by them, तु indeed, क्षोभिता agitated, नर्मदा the Narmada, नदी river, वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैः by Vamana, Anjana, Padma, and others, गङ्गा the Ganga, इव like, महागजैः by great elephants.
explanation: The Narmada river was agitated by those chief Rakshasas, who were like great elephants, just as the Ganga is disturbed by great elephants like Vamana, Anjana, and Padma.

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा नर्मदायां महाबलाः । उत्तीर्य पुष्पाण्याजह्रुर्बल्यर्थं रावणस्य तु ।। 7.31.36 ।।
transliteration: tataste rākṣasāḥ snātvā narmadāyāṃ mahābalāḥ | uttīrya puṣpāṇyājahrurbalyarthaṃ rāvaṇasya tu || 7.31.36 ||
translation: ततः then, ते those, राक्षसाः Rākṣasas, स्नात्वा having bathed, नर्मदायाम् in the Narmada, महाबलाः mighty, उत्तीर्य having come out, पुष्पाणि flowers, आजह्रुः brought, बल्यर्थम् for the offering, रावणस्य of Ravana, तु indeed.
explanation: Then, those mighty Rākṣasas, having bathed in the Narmada and emerged from the water, brought flowers for Ravana's offering.

shloka_text: नर्मदापुलिने हृद्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे । राक्षसैस्तु मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः ।। 7.31.37 ।।
transliteration: narmadāpuline hṛdye śubhrābhrasadṛśaprabhe | rākṣasaistu muhūrtena kṛtaḥ puṣpamayo giriḥ || 7.31.37 ||
translation: नर्मदापुलिने on the sandbank of the Narmada, हृद्ये charming, शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे having a luster like a white cloud, राक्षसैः by the Rākṣasas, तु indeed, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, कृतः was made, पुष्पमयः made of flowers, गिरिः a mountain.
explanation: On the charming sandbank of the Narmada, which shone like a white cloud, the Rākṣasas swiftly created a mountain of flowers in a moment.

shloka_text: पुष्पेषूपहृतेष्वेवं रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । अवतीर्णो नदीं स्नातुं गङ्गामिव महागजः ।। 7.31.38 ।।
transliteration: puṣpeṣūpahṛteṣvevaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ | avatīrṇo nadīṃ snātuṃ gaṅgāmiva mahāgajaḥ || 7.31.38 ||
translation: पुष्पेषु when the flowers, उपहृतेषु were brought, एवम् thus, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rākṣasas, अवतीर्णः descended, नदीम् into the river, स्नातुम् to bathe, गङ्गाम् into the Ganga, इव like, महागजः a great elephant.
explanation: When the flowers were thus brought, Ravana, the lord of Rākṣasas, descended into the river to bathe, just like a great elephant entering the Ganga.

shloka_text: तत्र स्नात्वा च विधिवज्जप्त्वा जप्यमनुत्तमम् । नर्मदासलिलात्तस्मादुत्ततार स रावणः ।। 7.31.39 ।।
transliteration: tatra snātvā ca vidhivajjaptvā japyamanuttamam | narmadāsalilāttasmāduttatāra sa rāvaṇaḥ || 7.31.39 ||
translation: तत्र there, स्नात्वा having bathed, च and, विधिवत् according to ritual, जप्त्वा having recited, जप्यम् the mantra, अनुत्तमम् excellent, नर्मदासलिलात् from the waters of the Narmada, तस्मात् from that, उत्ततार he emerged, सः that, रावणः Ravana.
explanation: Having bathed there according to ritual and recited the excellent mantra, that Ravana then emerged from the waters of the Narmada.

shloka_text: ततः क्लिन्नाम्बरं त्यक्त्वा शुक्लवस्त्रसमावृतम् । रावणं प्राञ्जलिं यान्तमन्वयुः सर्वराक्षसाः ।। 7.31.40 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ klinnāmbaraṃ tyaktvā śuklavastrasamāvṛtam | rāvaṇaṃ prāñjaliṃ yāntamanvayuḥ sarvarākṣasāḥ || 7.31.40 ||
translation: ततः then, क्लिन्नाम्बरम् wet garment, त्यक्त्वा having discarded, शुक्लवस्त्रसमावृतम् covered with white garments, रावणम् Ravana, प्राञ्जलिम् with folded hands, यान्तम् going, अन्वयुः followed, सर्वराक्षसाः all the Rākṣasas.
explanation: Then, having discarded his wet garment and now clad in white, Ravana proceeded with folded hands, followed by all the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: तद्गतीवशमापन्ना मूर्तिमन्त इवाचलाः । यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते ।। 7.31.41 ।।
transliteration: tadgatīvaśamāpannā mūrtimanta ivācalāḥ | yatra yatra ca yāti sma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ | jāmbūnadamayaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra tatra sma nīyate || 7.31.41 ||
translation: तद्गतीवशमापन्ना having come under the sway of his movement, मूर्तिमन्तः embodied, इव as if, अचलाः mountains, यत्र यत्र wherever, च and, याति स्म went, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसेश्वरः the lord of Rakshasas, जाम्बूनदमयम् made of pure gold, लिङ्गम् the Lingam, तत्र तत्र there, स्म नीयते was carried.
explanation: Wherever Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, went, the golden Shiva Lingam, as if an embodied mountain that had come under the sway of his movement, was carried along with him.

shloka_text: वालुकावेदिमध्ये तु तल्लिङ्गं स्थाप्य रावणः । अर्चयामास गन्धैश्च पुष्पैश्चामृतगन्धिभिः ।। 7.31.42 ।।
transliteration: vālukāvedimadhye tu talliṅgaṃ sthāpya rāvaṇaḥ | arcayāmāsa gandhaiśca puṣpaiścāmṛtagandhibhiḥ || 7.31.42 ||
translation: वालुकावेदिमध्ये in the middle of a sand altar, तु indeed, तल्लिङ्गम् that Lingam, स्थाप्य having placed, रावणः Ravana, अर्चयामास worshipped, गन्धैः with fragrances, च and, पुष्पैः with flowers, च and, अमृतगन्धिभिः having the fragrance of nectar.
explanation: Ravana placed that Lingam in the middle of a sand altar and worshipped it with fragrant substances and flowers that smelled like nectar.

shloka_text: ततः सतामार्तिहरं परं वरं वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम् । समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ प्रसार्य हस्तान्प्रणनर्त चाग्रतः ।। 7.31.43 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ satāmārtiharaṃ paraṃ varaṃ varapradaṃ candramayūkhabhūṣaṇam | samarcayitvā sa niśācaro jagau prasārya hastānpraṇanarta cāgrataḥ || 7.31.43 ||
translation: ततः then, सताम् of the good, आर्तिहरम् the remover of distress, परम् the supreme, वरम् boon (or best one), वरप्रदम् the giver of boons, चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम् adorned with moonbeams, समर्चयित्वा having worshipped well, सः he, निशाचरः the night-wanderer (Ravana), जगौ sang, प्रसार्य having stretched out, हस्तान् his hands, प्रणनर्त danced, च and, अग्रतः in front.
explanation: Then, having worshipped Shiva, who removes the distress of the virtuous, is the supreme boon, grants boons, and is adorned with the moon's rays, Ravana, the night-wanderer, sang and danced in front of the deity with outstretched hands. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 31 ।। Thus ends the thirty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
